items.title: JPJ seizes 3,790 luxury vehicles worth RM550m in nationwide crackdown since June 2025
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 27 — A total of 3,790 luxury vehicles worth an estimated RM550 million were seized by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) under Ops Luxury from June 2025 to yesterday for various offences. JPJ senior director of enforcement Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said 785 vehicles were seized between June and December 2025, while another 3,005 were seized from January to September 26 this year. “Some luxury vehicle owners said they were reluctant to go to JPJ offices to renew their road tax because they had been blacklisted for previous offences.

items.title: 10 missing after avalanche hits Nepal's Himlung peak base camp
items.summary: KATHMANDU: At least 10 local climbers and guides are missing after an avalanche hit the base camp of Himlung peak in central Nepal early Sunday, an expedition organiser said. "Eight members of our expedition team and two more from another company have been reported missing," Thakur said, adding that all those missing are Nepali. Heavy snowfall on Manaslu this week forced climbers to cancel expeditions.

items.title: A month without answers: Families of missing Malaysians told Nepal search may soon end
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 27 — After more than a month of waiting without news, the families of Malaysians still missing following the flood disaster in Nepal are beginning to resign themselves to all possibilities when informed that the government of that country is considering ending the search and rescue (SAR) operations. S. Sankara, the son of a missing Malaysian, said Wisma Putra informed them that the Nepalese government is expected to conclude the rescue operation phase soon before transitioning to recovery operations. “Based on the briefing received, the search and rescue operation is still ongoing at this time.

items.title: Heavy rain kills 56 in India's Uttar Pradesh
items.summary: LUCKNOW: Heavy rain triggered floods and landslides in the northern Indian state of Uttar Pradesh, killing at least 56 people over the past three days, a government disaster agency said on Sunday. Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state with more than 240 million people, is frequently battered by rain and thunderstorms during the annual monsoon season from June to September. The latest deaths were reported during a spell of "exceptionally heavy rain that has affected much of Uttar Pradesh", the Relief Commissioner's office said in a statement.

items.title: Dr Wan Azizah wants women to make up at least 30pc of PKR candidates in Melaka
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 27 — The principle of justice must continue to be the cornerstone of PKR’s struggle as it faces the Melaka state election, said the party’s Advisory Council chairman Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail. That is what we uphold in our party and in our struggle,” she told reporters after launching the Melaka Wanita PKR election machinery here today. Also present were prime minister’s political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin and Melaka Wanita PKR chief Mahani Masban.

items.title: Bangkok floods: Malaysians advised to register with e-Konsular
items.summary: BANGKOK: Malaysians in Bangkok have been urged to remain in contact with the Malaysian Embassy for assistance and updates following extensive flooding that affected several districts and major transportation routes in the capital city. The Foreign Ministry, in an advisory on Sunday, said several Malaysians had been affected by the floods, and that the Embassy in Bangkok was extending necessary support and assistance to them. It said Malaysians requiring consular assistance, or those with information on other Malaysians who may be affected by the floods, can contact the Embassy of Malaysia in Bangkok at +66 2 340 5720, +66 2 340 5731 or +66 87 028 4659, or email mwbangkok@kln.gov.my.

items.title: MCMC blocked 101.66 million spoof calls from Feb to Aug
items.summary: KULAI:The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in collaboration with telecommunications service providers, blocked a total of 101.66 million scam or spoof calls from Feb to Aug. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said this was achieved through the implementation of the Inter Operator Spoofing Gateway initiative, which has been in place since the beginning of this year. She said this when asked to comment on the number of scam calls blocked so far. Meanwhile, Teo said the MCMC will hold an online meeting with Meta tomorrow regarding public complaints concerning blocked WhatsApp accounts.

items.title: Families of 55 missing Malaysians in Nepal want moratorium to ease loans, insurance claims
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 27 — Families of 55 Malaysians still missing following the flash flood in Nepal have urged the government to consider a special moratorium on the victims’ financial commitments, as their families are now facing difficulties accessing the victims’ accounts and assets, insurance coverage, and managing their loans. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesperson Dr Manivannan Rethinam said that after 33 days without certainty, financial and legal issues have become among the most pressing concerns for the families, particularly as some of the victims were the main breadwinners. Manivannan said the victims’ status as missing persons had placed various constraints on their families, as assets and financial commitments under their names could not be managed as usual.

items.title: Amanah sets sights on 18 seats for GE16, but concedes it could lose all but one
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Sept 27 — Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) will identify its general election candidates early to allow them to introduce themselves to voters and to enable the party to make more systematic preparations. The party’s deputy president, Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa, said this move alongside strengthening the party’s machinery and narrative is crucial for Amanah to retain its existing seats and achieve its target of winning more seats in the 16th general election (GE16). He said Amanah aims to win at least 18 parliamentary seats in GE16, enabling the party to play a greater role in championing the interests of the ummah (Muslim community).

items.title: MCMC blocks 101.66 million scam calls with telcos under spoofing gateway from Feb to Aug
items.summary: KULAI, Sept 27 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in collaboration with telecommunications service providers, blocked a total of 101.66 million scam or spoof calls from February to August. She said this when asked to comment on the number of scam calls blocked so far. Meanwhile, Teo said the MCMC will hold an online meeting with Meta tomorrow regarding public complaints concerning blocked WhatsApp accounts.

items.title: Families of 55 missing in Nepal seek Anwar's help over death declaration
items.summary: Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the families were seeking a special exception for the 55 Malaysians, given the scale and circumstances of the disaster. Earlier, Dr Manivannan said the families faced a seven-year wait before a death declaration can be produced. Dr Manivannan said the families could explore other legal avenues, such as bringing the issue to the courts.

items.title: Calls unanswered, woman forces entry and finds fiancé dead in Melaka home
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 27 — A woman was left heartbroken after finding her fiancé lying lifeless in his home, having failed to reach him since last night. The 38-year-old went to his house in Simpang Ampat around 11am today after growing anxious when her calls went unanswered, Harian Metro (HM) reported. Alor Gajah district police chief Superintendent Ahmad Abu Bakar said she had gone to the man’s residence to look for him after being unable to contact him.

items.title: Diversification, regional resilience will ensure Malacca Strait relevance
items.summary: LETTER: Global trade is entering a new phase as a shipping corridor through the Arctic Ocean, which is known as the Northern Sea Route (NSR), promoted as a quicker alternative to the traditional maritime transit through Suez. Due to the high-risk zone of the Arctic, insurance premiums are higher. At the same time, Russia, which controls the NSR, also charges navigation and pilotage fees.

items.title: MetMalaysia alerts seven states to evening thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds
items.summary: In Perak, the affected area is Hulu Perak, while in Kelantan, the warning covers Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang and Pasir Puteh, MetMalaysia said in a statement. The warning also covers Besut, Setiu, Dungun, Kemaman, Marang and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; Pekan, Rompin and Jerantut in Pahang; and Kota Tinggi and Mersing in Johor. In Sabah, the warning covers the West Coast (Ranau, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Kota Belud, Penampang and Papar), Interior (Keningau, Tambunan, Pensiangan, Sook, Tenom, Sipitang, Beaufort and Membakut), Kudat (Kota Marudu), and Sandakan (Kinabatangan and Sandakan).

items.title: Johor haze likely linked to smoke from southern Sumatra
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Smoke from fires in Indonesia's southern Sumatra is believed to be contributing to the haze blanketing Johor, with prevailing winds carrying transboundary smoke across the Malacca Strait into southern Peninsular Malaysia. The Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) reported that moderate to dense smoke plumes were observed emanating from hotspot clusters in southern Sumatra, while haze from the region had also been observed moving towards Singapore and southern Peninsular Malaysia. The pattern suggests the haze has shifted towards southern Peninsular Malaysia, with transboundary smoke from southern Sumatra a likely contributor.

items.title: School must be a place of safety, not fear
items.summary: We have spoken repeatedly about bullying and violence in schools. I urge the Education Ministry and schools to strengthen preventive measures, particularly in hostels: • Strengthen supervision, especially during after-school and night-time hours. • Train teachers, wardens and school administrators to recognise early signs of bullying, intimidation and violent behaviour.

items.title: Evening haze: Unhealthy air quality in five areas nationwide, Johor accounts for four and Sarawak one
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Five areas, four in Johor and one in Sarawak, recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at an unhealthy level as of 4pm today. Meanwhile, in Sarawak, only Serian recorded an unhealthy API reading, at 141. A total of 51 areas, including Kuala Lumpur, recorded readings at a moderate level, while 12 areas recorded good readings.

items.title: Malaysians missing in Nepal: Families face 7-year wait for death declaration
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The families of 55 Malaysians still missing following the disaster in Nepal are facing a seven-year wait before they can seek a declaration of death, leaving them in prolonged legal and financial limbo. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the National Registration Department told the families that the Nepalese government would first have to make a declaration, followed by a statement from the Nepalese embassy. Dr Manivannan said the wait could have serious financial consequences for families already struggling to meet commitments.

items.title: Global South must have greater say in AI-goverance - Mohamad Hasan
items.summary: NEW YORK: The Global South must have a meaningful role in shaping decisions on artificial intelligence (AI) rather than merely becoming a destination for data centres, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said. He said AI was transforming economies, societies and government decision-making, thus creating enormous opportunities but also significant risks. Mohamad said the UN must continue empowering Global South countries, which are likely to be more greatly affected by inequitable AI development, to participate in global discussions on AI.

items.title: Nepal disaster: SMART did not search Rasuwagadhi due to operational constraints
items.summary: This was conveyed by SMART commander Abdul Manaf Che Isa to families of the 55 Malaysians who remain uncontactable in Nepal, during a briefing at Wisma Putra today. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the families had sought an explanation on why SMART did not search the Rasuwagadhi area, which was among locations believed to be relevant to the missing Malaysians. However, he said Nepal has yet to start processing the DNA samples.

items.title: Do not compare Penang’s mega projects with one year of Sabah road funding, state PKR tells PAS rival
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 27 — Transport infrastructure development in Sabah remains a priority for the Madani Government, with comparisons between states needing to take into account their respective scale and requirements, said Sabah PKR Information Chief Ahmad Farid Sainuri. He said Sabah’s roads still required serious attention, including faster completion of the Pan Borneo Highway to narrow the development gap between Sabah and Peninsular Malaysia. “We do not deny that Sabah’s roads still require serious attention.

items.title: Thousands seek to thwart disputed N.Ireland flashpoint parade
items.summary: The tensions spiked after a court in the early hours of Sunday cleared the march by the Orange Order to go ahead. The Parades Commission, Northern Ireland's independent body regulating contentious processions, had authorised 35 Orangemen to march silently along Garvaghy Road in Portadown, without bands or supporters from 8am (0700 GMT) Sunday. About 2,000 people walked early Sunday in the Garvaghy Road area of Portadown, 25 miles southwest of Belfast, in a counter-protest seeking to prevent the Orange march.

items.title: Nepal floods: DNA samples from families of Malaysians yet to be processed, says group
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: DNA samples provided by families of 55 Malaysians still missing in Nepal have yet to be processed, according to Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam. "So far, they haven't processed even one yet. He said the samples were collected in preparation for comparison with DNA extracted from any remains recovered in Nepal.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain forecast in 7 states
items.summary: In Perak, the affected area is Hulu Perak, while in Kelantan, the warning covers Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang and Pasir Puteh, MetMalaysia said in a statement. The warning also covers Besut, Setiu, Dungun, Kemaman, Marang and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; Pekan, Rompin and Jerantut in Pahang; and Kota Tinggi and Mersing in Johor. In Sabah, the warning covers the West Coast (Ranau, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Kota Belud, Penampang and Papar), Interior (Keningau, Tambunan, Pensiangan, Sook, Tenom, Sipitang, Beaufort and Membakut), Kudat (Kota Marudu), and Sandakan (Kinabatangan and Sandakan).

items.title: Armizan hopes for more Rahmah sales allocation in 2027 Budget
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali hopes that the allocation for Madani Rahmah Sales Programme (Jualan Rahmah) can be increased in the 2027 Budget to allow the programme to be further expanded and benefit more people. Armizan said that with the specific allocation established starting from the 2024 Budget, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry has been able to set annual and monthly implementation targets and expand public access to Rahmah Sales. Meanwhile, Armizan said public access to information regarding Rahmah Sales events has also been improved in tandem with the expanded scale of the programme's implementation.

items.title: BN chairman Zahid says coalition will end ties with Pakatan once Parliament dissolves
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today made he saw no possibility of cooperation between his coalition and Pakatan Harapan (PH), amid talks that relations between the two sides have hit “an all time low”. Speaking at the 18th annual general assembly of the Malaysian Makkal Sakti Party at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur this afternoon, the Umno president “promised” that BN would “part ways” the moment Parliament is dissolved, in an apparent response to calls for the coalition to stop all forms of political cooperation with PH in the Unity Government. At the same event, Parti Makkal Sakti Malaysia president Datuk Seri RS Thanenthiran urged Zahid to pull BN out of the Unity government as soon as possible.

items.title: Fire Dept finds nine tiny rooms squeezed into office and turned into student dormitory in Terengganu
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 27 — Small student dormitories built within an office premises were among the conditions detected today by the Terengganu Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) during the Ops Sepadu Premis Sarang Burung operation around Kuala Terengganu. The premises on the second floor had nine small rooms built separately and converted into student dormitories, in addition to being found non-compliant with several building safety regulations. The integrated operation was carried out at four locations, namely Jalan Masjid Abidin, Jalan Engku Pengiran Anom 2, Jalan Engku Sar and Jalan Sultan Zainal Abidin.

items.title: 132 Kemas preschools for children with autism to begin operation in January
items.summary: MELAKA: A total of 132 Community Development Department (Kemas) preschools (Tabika) for children with autism will begin operations next January. "If we look at the Education Ministry, children in these special classes receive an allowance as special-needs children. TAGS: Kemas, preschool, allowance, operation, autism, children, parents, PwD, Welfare Department, Education Ministry, Malaysia, news, NST © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Perlis Raja Muda visits learning centre in MAIPs programme
items.summary: KANGAR: Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail visited the Community Learning Centre (CLBC) in Kampung Seberang Ramai, Kuala Perlis yesterday, accompanied by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, as part of the Kayuhan MAIPs Peduli programme organised by the Perlis Islamic Religious and Malay Customs Council (MAIPs). Perlis state secretary Datuk Noor Azman Abdul Rahman, Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and MAIPs chief executive officer Mohd Nazim Mohd Noor were also part of the visit. [[nid:1542302]] Istana Arau, in a statement today, said that during the visit, Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra observed an ongoing English tuition class involving students from the local community.

items.title: Kemas expands preschool places for children with autism, 132 classes to open nationwide in Jan 2027
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 27 — A total of 132 Community Development Department (Kemas) preschools for children with autism will open nationwide next January, with admission screening set to begin next month. Kemas director-general Datuk Mohd Hanafiah Man said the screening would be conducted in collaboration with the Ministry of Health. “If we look at the Ministry of Education, children in these special classes receive an allowance as special-needs children.

items.title: Police target dark, abandoned and neglected spots in nationwide crime drive, starting with Penang
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 27 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will expand its Whitening The Black Spot initiative nationwide in stages, beginning with Penang, said Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail. Also present were Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin, Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng and Mohd Khalid’s wife Puan Sri Munirah Che Rose. Mohd Khalid said the Penang phase will run for a month before being expanded to black spots in other states battling high crime rates or pressing security issues.

items.title: Police declare major incident at UK's Fairford air base, used by US air forces
items.summary: LONDON: British police said on Sunday they had arrested several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act and the army was examining a number of vehicles after security was stepped up at a British air base used by US air forces in southwest England. A Reuters eyewitness said armed police were blocking access to the main gate of the base. A spokesperson for the US Air Force said they would not discuss specific force protection measures.

items.title: BN to weigh PAS contesting under coalition logo as Melaka election talks intensify
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will discuss this week a proposal for PAS to contest under the coalition’s logo in the upcoming Melaka state election. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the matter would be decided after consultations with Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh and other parties, Harian Metro (HM) reported. Yesterday, Perikatan Nasional (PN) secretary general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, who is also PAS secretary general, said the coalition had not ruled out using the PAS logo or those of other component parties in Melaka if PN’s suspension remained in effect.

items.title: Malaysia to ship out 578 more e-waste containers as border agency targets full clearance by end 2026
items.summary: SEGAMAT, Sept 27 — The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) has re-exported 436 containers of electronic waste (e-waste) to their countries of origin this year, with another 578 containers due to be sent out from October. The agency said the operations were carried out in collaboration with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), Royal Malaysia Police, Department of Environment, and port authorities. Meanwhile, AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said the agency had recorded seizures worth RM265.89 million this year, about three times the value recorded in 2025.

items.title: Govt chief secretary pitches training academy for border agents as Malaysia faces more complex threats
items.summary: SEGAMAT, Sept 27 — The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) needs its own world-class training academy to build expertise in border management technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Dr Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said today. He said building in-house capabilities was crucial for preparing AKPS officers to tackle increasingly complex border security challenges and operate independently over the next 10 to 20 years. Shamsul Azri said the proposed academy was part of AKPS’ plan to move beyond securing entry points towards smart, integrated and intelligence-led border control.

items.title: Immigration raids same-sex entertainment centre in KL
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department uncovered activities at an entertainment centre in the capital featuring dance performances by individuals of the same gender during a special operation early this morning. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said during the joint operation with the National Anti-Drug Agency, which began at 12.05am, three Chinese nationals and one Filipino national — all male and aged between 21 and 31 — were detained. Zakaria said the entertainment centre, located on Jalan Klang Lama and operational since last year, is believed to have offered entertainment and dance performances by foreigners of the same gender, targeting both local and foreign customers in the Klang Valley.

items.title: UiTM Holdings under MACC spotlight as RM42m solar project payment questioned
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 27 — The Malaysian Anti Corruption Commission (MACC) is investigating several issues linked to losses suffered by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd in 2023. “MACC will strive to complete the investigation swiftly, independently and fairly. Abd Halim said the commission welcomed the Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s concern and firm stance in addressing shortcomings that contributed to UiTM Holdings’ losses.

items.title: MCBA: Cannabis smuggling attempts foiled 'almost daily' at Malaysian airports
items.summary: SEGAMAT: Attempts to smuggle cannabis flowers out of Malaysia are being foiled almost daily at Kuala Lumpur International Airport, with foreigners making up most of those detained, the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) said today. Suhaily said almost every day, or at least every week, MCBA detained those attempting to smuggle cannabis flowers out of the country. He said MCBA was tasked with coordinating screening with Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) at both KLIA terminals.

items.title: MACC probes UiTM Holdings over 2023 losses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has launched an investigation into UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd over losses incurred by the company in 2023. "To complete the investigation, MACC will also examine whether there are other relevant issues, including governance weaknesses, as highlighted by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim," MACC said in a statement today. He said MACC would complete the investigation swiftly, independently and fairly.

items.title: Signalling fault throws KTM Komuter and ETS schedules off track, delays top five hours
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — A signalling system disruption between Kalumpang and Kuala Kubu Bharu yesterday delayed KTM Komuter and ETS services by up to five hours. In a statement today, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) said the worst KTM Komuter delay was recorded by Train No. The signalling fault during the works further restricted train movements and compounded delays to several KTM Komuter and ETS services, it said.

items.title: MCBA needs world-class training academy - Chief Secretary
items.summary: SEGAMAT: The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) needs its own world-class training academy to produce highly skilled officers in border management technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Dr Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar. "The world-class MCBA Training Academy is important for producing more talented and highly skilled Malaysians in border management technologies, including artificial intelligence, who are future-ready, uphold integrity and are committed to safeguarding national interests," he said at the passing-out ceremony for the MCBA Basic Training Course Series 1/2026 at the Segamat Police Training Centre (Pulapol) today. Also present was MCBA director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.

items.title: FBM KLCI futures set for bargain hunting on US-China trade truce extension
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) futures contract is expected to attract bargain-hunting interest next week, supported by the extension of the US-China trade truce by another two months. "Improved risk appetite following the extension of the trade truce could provide room for the index to rebound, although elevated oil prices and global bond yields remain key downside risks. The FBM KLCI futures ended lower this week, tracking the weaker underlying cash market.

items.title: China, US agree to US$30bil tariff cut, AI dialogue during Xi visit
items.summary: SHANGHAI: China said on Saturday it had agreed with the US on a US$30 billion reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement and on launching a dialogue on AI, under an eight-point consensus reached during President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington. The two sides have also agreed to set up a trade council and extend the outcomes of earlier talks in Kuala Lumpur, the Chinese Foreign Ministry said. The agreement follows an earlier move by the world's two largest economies to extend by two months a trade truce that had been due to expire on November 10, allowing more time to work on ‌a potentially bigger trade deal, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday.

items.title: Kelantan businesswoman's RM500,000 Jeep among 3,790 luxury vehicles seized
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A Jeep Wrangler worth nearly RM500,000 belonging to a popular Kelantan businesswoman was among 3,790 luxury vehicles seized by the Road Transport Department nationwide under Op Luxury. He said the 3,790 vehicles were seized between June 2025 and Sept 26 this year, with an estimated value of RM550 million. Of the total, Kifli said 785 vehicles were seized between June and December last year, while another 3,005 were seized from Jan 1 to Sept 26 this year.

items.title: Beyond the F1 circuit, Bagan Lalang offers a slower side of Sepang
items.summary: At Pantai Bagan Lalang, just about 30 minutes away from the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), the sound of waves replaces roaring engines as campers pitch their tents along the coast, drawn by the beach's open views and its location at the meeting point of the sea and river. For Chef Yang, 56, who has lived in Sepang since 2000, the beach has become a regular camping ground over the past five years. "I camp almost every day," she said, adding that she preferred Bagan Lalang because of its location at the estuary, where she can watch the sunset and observe fishing boats coming and going.

items.title: Chairman: 'UiTM Holdings has recovery plan to address losses'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd already has a recovery plan and proposals to address its financial position following accumulated losses of RM157 million, said its chairman Datuk Dr Fathul Bari Mat Jahya. Fathul Bari said he acknowledged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's concerns over the losses incurred by UiTM Holdings Group. He said the past losses had created a trust deficit in UiTM Holdings.

items.title: Signalling disruption causes up to 5-hour delays for KTM Komuter, ETS
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A signalling system disruption between Kalumpang and Kuala Kubu Baru yesterday left KTM Komuter and ETS services delayed by up to five hours. In a statement today, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) said KTM Komuter's worst delay hit Train No. KTMB said preliminary checks traced the disruption to damage in a system component, which sparked and disrupted the signalling system.

items.title: Zahid brings rival camps together to find way out of Negeri Sembilan crisis, says no need to declare political emergency for now
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today said he will hold a meeting tonight with Negeri Sembilan assemblymen from Barisan Nasional (BN), PAS and Parti Wawasan Negara tonight in a fresh attempt to resolve the state’s ongoing constitutional crisis. Zahid, who is BN chairman, said any solution must put the interests of the people first while respecting the state’s laws, Constitution and customs. Zahid was also asked about the possibility of declaring a political emergency in Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: Sepang businesses eye F1 windfall as race returns after nine years
items.summary: When the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix takes place at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) from Oct 2-4, thousands of motorsport fans, racing teams and international visitors are expected to descend on the district. Sepang member of parliament Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said the race's return was expected to generate significant economic spillover for Sepang and surrounding areas, particularly in tourism, hospitality, transport, food and beverage, and small businesses. "F1 is not merely a racing event, but a platform to promote Malaysia, particularly Sepang, as a world-class tourism destination," she said.

items.title: 'Once Parliament is dissolved, we are no longer with them' - Zahid
items.summary: That was the assurance from Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi on the coalition's commitment to the unity government, which he said would end when the 15th Parliament is dissolved. Zahid said BN had decided to join the unity government after the 15th general election (GE15) and would honour that commitment until the end of the parliamentary term. After GE15, Barisan Nasional decided to be part of the government, and our commitment is to remain in the government until the end of the 15th Parliament.

items.title: Zahid says Najib solidarity fund hits RM9.25m — still RM40.75m short of target
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — The Najib Razak Solidarity Fund has reached RM9.25 million nine days after its launch, but Umno is still short of the RM50 million needed to help the former prime minister meet the fine attached to his conditional pardon for house arrest. Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the latest amount was recorded as of 10am Saturday, leaving the fund RM40.75 million short of its target, The Star reported today. “This is still insufficient to reach the RM50 million target.

items.title: Way out of Negeri Sembilan impasse? MB Ismail Lasim should seek audience with Ruler and Undangs, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has urged Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to seek an audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir and the four Undangs to find a way out of the state’s constitutional crisis. Zahid, who is also Umno president, said he had asked Ismail to engage the state’s traditional chieftains and seek an amicable solution in accordance with the Negeri Sembilan Constitution and state customs, news outlet Free Malaysia Today reported this afternoon. Zahid also acknowledged Tuanku Muhriz’s decision to revoke the appointments of the 10 state executive councillors, saying the immediate priority was to ensure the state administration could continue serving the people.

items.title: Why RM21b for Penang transport while Sabah still waits on roads, Pan Borneo? PAS rep asks Putrajaya
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 27 — Parti Islam Se-Malaysia (PAS) Sabah has questioned the federal government’s transport infrastructure priorities, highlighting more than RM21 billion in approved transport projects in Penang while Sabah continues to face road maintenance needs and delays involving the Pan Borneo Highway. Its Information Chief Mustaman Mustain said the federal government should clarify its priorities, particularly given Sabah’s extensive road network and infrastructure needs. Mustaman said the federal government allocated RM341.7 million for federal road maintenance in Sabah in 2025, covering about 1,536.949km of federal roads under its maintenance jurisdiction.

items.title: Who checks tourist safety at Mengalum? Sabah reps seek answers after snorkelling death
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 27 — Authorities have been urged to clarify tourist safety measures, land status and regulatory oversight at Mengalum Island following the death of a Chinese tourist during a snorkelling activity on Sept 23. He said tourist safety should not rest with a single agency, calling for clearer coordination among Kota Kinabalu City Hall (DBKK), the Sabah Lands and Surveys Department, Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Environment Sabah (KePKAS), Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture Malaysia (Motac) and other relevant agencies. “We must also ask whether the tourism activities and facilities at the destination itself have the necessary approvals and whether the relevant safety procedures were properly implemented,” he said in a statement.

items.title: One-third formula first, more seats later, Sabah and Sarawak politicians tell Putrajaya
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 27 — Putrajaya must first work out the one-third formula for Sabah and Sarawak representation in the Dewan Rakyat before adding any parliamentary seats. “More seats do not necessarily strengthen Sabah and Sarawak if seats in Peninsular Malaysia also increase and the overall ratio remains largely unchanged. The real issue, therefore, is not how many seats are added, but what proportion of parliamentary seats Sabah and Sarawak will ultimately hold,” he said.

items.title: Police to record statements from former exco members amid Negeri Sembilan royal turmoil
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 27 — The police will summon former Negeri Sembilan state executive council (Exco) members starting tomorrow and the day after to record their statements, to assist the investigation into the administrative and royal institution crisis in the state following several police reports lodged regarding the matter. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said in addition to the Exco members, the police would also take statements from several witnesses and other relevant individuals to complete the investigation. Mohd Khalid made these remarks when asked to comment on the police investigation into the administrative and royal institution crisis in Negeri Sembilan from various angles, following several police reports lodged regarding the issue.

items.title: MetMalaysia keeps 24‑hour watch on Sabah quakes via 28 seismic stations
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 27 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MET Malaysia) is keeping a round-the-clock watch on earthquake activity in Sabah via 28 seismic stations statewide. MET Malaysia director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the monitoring enables the department to detect and analyse earthquakes swiftly. He said the seismic stations closest to the epicentre are Sapulut, 57.23 kilometres away; Keningau (66.51 kilometres); Sandakan/Telupid (74.36 kilometres); Matupang (76.67 kilometres); and Tenom (93.32 kilometres).

items.title: Dungun religious teacher remanded after three boys lodge sexual assault reports
items.summary: DUNGUN, Sept 27 — A former mudir (headmaster) of a tahfiz school here has been remanded for five days from today to assist investigations into the alleged sexual assault of three male students, aged 13 and 14, in incidents between April and September last year. District police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said the remand order was issued by Magistrate Ng Yan Ni to facilitate investigations under Sections 14(b) and 14(d) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017. “Police received three reports regarding the incidents yesterday, and preliminary investigations found that all three victims were former students of the school in 2025,” he said when contacted.

items.title: Foreign Ministry advises Malaysians in Bangkok to stay connected with embassy
items.summary: BANGKOK, Sept 27 — Malaysians in Bangkok have been urged to remain in contact with the Malaysian Embassy for assistance and updates following extensive flooding that affected several districts and major transportation routes in the capital city. The Foreign Ministry, in an advisory on Sunday, said several Malaysians had been affected by the floods, and that the Embassy in Bangkok was extending necessary support and assistance to them. It said Malaysians requiring consular assistance, or those with information on other Malaysians who may be affected by the floods, can contact the Embassy of Malaysia in Bangkok at +66 2 340 5720, +66 2 340 5731 or +66 87 028 4659, or email mwbangkok@kln.gov.my .

items.title: Foreign male dancers nabbed as Immigration raids Jalan Klang Lama club charging patrons up to RM700
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Immigration officers raided an entertainment centre in Jalan Klang Lama offering dance shows by foreign men during a special operation early Saturday. Immigration director general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the raid began at 12.05am following a month of surveillance and public tip offs, Sinar Harian (SH) reported. Zakaria said the Immigration Department will continue joint operations with other enforcement agencies to curb illegal activities.
